teams.heading: Ikanivere's second-half double turns 13-7 deficit into Fiji's 21-16 win over Italy
teams.body: Saturday's 21-16 win in Udine turned after the interval, when Ikanivere struck twice, according to Rugbyrama, which judged Italy deserving of their 13-7 half-time lead after dominating the first period. Reuters framed it as Fiji's first Nations Championship victory, and FBC News saw a Flying Fijians side showing progress in a hard-fought win. Rugbyrama noted that the result still leaves Jake White's men bottom of their pool, the same place Italy finish, with the closing weekend at Twickenham to come.

lead.why: The only new item, and it adds the match-turning detail of Ikanivere's second-half brace to Fiji's win.

teams.heading: Borthwick mined Eddie Jones footage behind England's fast start in 37-12 win
teams.body: Henry Slade's fourth-minute try in Saturday's 37-12 win over New Zealand was no accident. Steve Borthwick said he has watched videos from Eddie Jones's time in charge to help England begin matches strongly. He and his assistants had identified slow starts as a key factor in England's slump earlier in the year. The fix has held, with England scoring the opening try inside seven minutes in all three matches this month. Will Joseph crossed within the first minute of the 78-15 rout of Japan.

lead.why: Freeman's injury and the record margin have already run, so this is the freshest England story: Borthwick's own method behind the result.

teams.heading: Kalvin Gourgues kicks 5 from 6 on goal-kicking bow in 45-17 win
teams.body: The 21-year-old centre also scored twice against the Pumas on Saturday. He was handed the tee despite never having kicked at international level, and he had kicked only once in the Top 14. Fabien Galthié explained that France had set off without a recognised goal-kicker, joking that Gourgues had now lost his 100% record. Antoine Dupont, his Toulouse teammate, said the responsibility had not unsettled him. Gourgues admitted he loves kicking and has been practising after sessions with Maxime Petitjean and the other kickers.

lead.why: The squad recall has already run, and the new goal-kicker's performance in Saturday's win is the freshest France match story.

teams.heading: The42 credits Ireland's bold passing against Springbok blitz in 20-17 win
teams.body: Andy Farrell's side pushed passes into South Africa's linespeed rather than shying away from it, The42's analysis argues, and the tone was set on Saturday's first attack. Off a three-man pod, Ryan Baird swept the ball out the back to Sam Prendergast, whose dummy to Robbie Henshaw held up Cameron Hanekom before he released the centre through Morné van den Berg's grasp into the South Africa 22. On the very next phase, Jamison Gibson-Park fizzed a pass across Prendergast's face to buy Stuart McCloskey time.

lead.why: The top-ranked new item gives a fresh tactical angle on the Springbok win, distinct from the Baloucoune scoring story already run.

teams.heading: Sarugbymag says 16-21 Fiji loss capped Quesada's winless Nations Championship campaign
teams.body: Saturday's 16-21 defeat in Udine drew broadly even-handed verdicts abroad, but South Africa's Sarugbymag.co.za was the bluntest, calling it the end of a disappointing season for Quesada's Italy, six losses from six, ahead of the finals weekend at Twickenham. AP News and Reuters framed it as Fiji's first Nations Championship win; Rugbyrama noted Italy led 13-7 at the break before Ikanivere's second-half double turned it. TNT Sports' headline cast both sides as teams in difficulty.

lead.why: The rankings slide and the post-match quotes have already run, so the foreign press verdict on the Fiji defeat is the freshest Italy story left.

teams.heading: Scotland U20 edge Ireland 31-29 in Cork as Dalrymple and Caldwell score
teams.body: Scotland U20 owed Friday's win at Musgrave Park to steadier goal-kicking, overcoming an Ireland side who scored five tries behind a dominant scrum and maul. Ireland crossed twice while centre Harry Soboil was in the bin, but their own indiscipline brought cards for Jonny Ginnety and Bernard White, and Scotland struck through wing Rory Caldwell, second row James Dalrymple and lock Christian Lindsay. Ireland's Paul Neary then watched a late conversion that would have levelled it drift wide.

lead.why: The senior rout and the Fagerson injury have both run, so the U20 win in Cork is the only fresh Scotland result available.

teams.heading: Liam Botham says Tandy got it wrong dropping James for 26-29 loss
teams.body: James Botham was left out of the 23 for Saturday's 26-29 defeat by Australia, a week after his 30-tackle, player-of-the-match display against New Zealand, with Cardiff colleague Alex Mann preferred. His father, a self-declared "massive supporter" of Tandy, asked on LinkedIn: "How do you leave him out after a performance like that?" Tandy had said Botham's impending fatherhood played no part, citing workloads after nearly 350 tackles: "We have depth and genuine competition, so it was always the plan to freshen things up."

lead.why: A fresh row over a Wales selection call, reported by WalesOnline and the BBC, which is the story fans are talking about.

teams.heading: Pumas' Twickenham finale against Scotland: BBC's Tom English wants McConnell let loose
teams.body: Argentina's last assignment of the Nations Championship is a fourth-v-fourth meeting with Gregor Townsend's side, the warm-up act before the France-South Africa final. Writing for BBC Sport, Tom English singled out Liam McConnell after he and Darcy Graham each scored hat-tricks in Saturday's 11-try rout of an understrength Japan. He also flagged Scotland's seven first-half penalties in that game. Scotland lost at home to the Pumas in November before winning in Argentina in July.

teams.heading: Les Kiss flags 14 conceded penalties in 29-26 win before Ireland reunion
teams.body: Kiss has warned that discipline must improve before his Wallabies meet Ireland, the side whose defence he organised between 2009 and 2015. "The discipline was a little bit disappointing, I must say, it kept Wales in the game with field position," he said of Saturday's Cardiff Test. Taniela Tupou summed up the night: a try, a turnover and scrum dominance, but four first-half penalties. Ireland arrive fresh from a 20-17 win over South Africa, and Australia have lost their last six Tests against them.

lead.why: Kiss's discipline warning and Ireland reunion is the freshest Wallabies angle beyond the already-run Wales result.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones' nine-change Japan side swept aside 67-5 at Murrayfield
teams.body: Saturday's Murrayfield Test finished 67-5 to Scotland, Jones having made nine changes after the 78-15 loss to England. The entire front row was new — Sojiro Otsuka, Kenji Sato and Ryosuke Iwaihara — as were fly-half Shinya Komura and the centre pairing of Charlie Lawrence and Jisu Lee. The rebuilt side trailed 29-0 at the break, and only Takuro Matsunaga's 52nd-minute try kept Japan off nil.

lead.why: Jones' nine-change selection, judged by the result, is the one Japan angle not yet run.

teams.heading: New Zealand Rugby backs Dave Rennie after 37-12 England defeat at Twickenham
teams.body: The union has publicly stood by its head coach after successive defeats by Wales and England. The second, a 37-12 loss, was the most points the All Blacks have conceded in a Test against a Northern Hemisphere nation. Rennie conceded his team were 'miles off' and that London was worse than Cardiff. In the Herald, Gregor Paul recalled that last year's defeat by England ultimately led to Scott Robertson's removal. The All Blacks now face England again at Twickenham in the Nations Championship third-place final.

lead.why: The governing body backing the head coach after two straight defeats is a fresh decision about New Zealand, not more pundit reaction.

teams.heading: Assistants Jones and Stick deny banned Rassie fed instructions in 20-17 loss
teams.body: Questions followed Saturday's 20-17 defeat to Ireland after Erasmus — serving a six-Test suspension that bars match-day contact with his staff — was seen speaking into earbuds with his mouth covered during his watch-along from the team hotel. Asked by Irish media, Felix Jones said: "No, I had the mics." Mzwandile Stick suggested Rassie may have been talking to his online followers instead. There have been calls for World Rugby to act.

lead.why: Bok coaches answering questions over whether banned Erasmus breached his suspension is a news event, not a pundit's verdict.
